definitions.explanation: A being of enormous size, either in mythology, fiction, or figurative description of a very large person.
A person of outstanding importance or achievement in a particular field. Used to praise someone's towering influence or legacy.

examples.japanese: {巨人|きょじん}が{現|あらわ}れた。
{神話|しんわ}には{巨人|きょじん}の{伝説|でんせつ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many legends of giants in mythology.

examples.japanese: {北欧|ほくおう}{神話|しんわ}では、{巨人|きょじん}と{神々|かみがみ}が{戦|たたか}う{物語|ものがたり}が{語|かた}られている。
examples.english: In Norse mythology, stories are told of giants battling the gods.

examples.japanese: {音楽|おんがく}{界|かい}の{巨人|きょじん}と{呼|よ}ばれた。
examples.english: He was called a titan of the music world.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{文学|ぶんがく}の{巨人|きょじん}だ。
examples.english: He is a giant of literature.

examples.japanese: {科学|かがく}の{巨人|きょじん}たちの{肩|かた}の{上|うえ}に{立|た}って、{私|わたし}たちは{前|まえ}に{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: Standing on the shoulders of the giants of science, we move forward.

notes:
USAGE:
Also the nickname of the Yomiuri Giants ({読売|よみうり}ジャイアンツ), Japan's most famous professional baseball team, commonly called {巨人|きょじん} in everyday conversation. Context usually makes the meaning clear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {巨人|きょじん}と{呼|よ}ばれる: to be called a giant
- ～{界|かい}の{巨人|きょじん}: titan of the ~ world
- {巨人|きょじん}{軍|ぐん}: the Giants (baseball team)
- {巨人|きょじん}{戦|せん}: Giants game
